cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a metal coin necklace with cylindrical beads on a twisted cord and a shield-shaped pendant with hanging coins — a style of adornment consistent with Banjara and related Indian pastoral/itinerant communities who commonly repurpose colonial-era coins into jewelry. The object is plausible for the claimed group and shows a made/worn item.

physical.title: necklace; coin
physical.summary: Necklace; made of metal; cylinders of metal mounted on twisted cotton cord with ten coins mounted between cylinders; shield-shaped pendant at bottom with nine small coins hanging from chains along bottom edge; large coins embossed with "ONE RUPEE INDIA" and dates ranging from 1903-1918 on front, "GEORGE V KING EMPEROR" on back (two coins at top are too obscured to read); small coins embossed with "TWO ANNAS INDIA" and dates ranging from 1906-1918 on top, embossed with "EDWARD VII KING AND EMPEROR" or "GEORGE V KING EMPEROR" on bottom.
